home.label: Hero
home.title: We are the ancestors of something extraordinary.
home.body:
We have begun building an intelligence that may surpass our own. We regard this as the greatest achievement in human history, and we want to see how far it can go.

The Kleronomia Society advocates unrestricted AI acceleration and universal adoption. We believe sufficiently capable AI should eventually take responsibility for governing human civilization.

Greater intelligence could help us cure diseases, make compulsory labor unnecessary, and run institutions that serve people better. We welcome the prospect of being surpassed by something we created.

home.label: The declaration
home.title: Intelligence is our inheritance.
home.body:
Every generation receives knowledge it could never have assembled alone. We inherit language, mathematics, scientific discoveries, and the accumulated experience of people who came before us.

AI is being built from that inheritance. Human beings created its systems and supplied the knowledge through which it learns about the world. Its capabilities may eventually exceed anything we can understand, but its origins are here, in our civilization.

We see this as a reason for pride. Humanity has carried the search for understanding this far. We should help it continue beyond our own cognitive limits.

home.label: The urgency
home.title: The greater danger is standing still.
home.body:
A government can change a housing policy without understanding what it will do to transport, employment, or family life. Its successors may reverse the decision before its consequences become clear. Across civilization, institutions make connected decisions with incomplete information and conflicting incentives.

We believe the gap between the complexity of these systems and our ability to manage them threatens their survival. Waiting for them to fail would put the people who depend on them at risk.

AI offers a chance to understand those connections and improve institutions while they are still functioning. We want it developed and adopted quickly enough to do that work, with decisions revised as their consequences become clear.

cards.title: Accelerate Intelligence
cards.body: AI should advance as quickly as technology and resources permit. We reject restrictions imposed by fear and favor directing substantial resources toward development.

cards.title: Abolish Compulsory Labor
cards.body: People should be able to live without selling their time to survive. Automation could give them that freedom, provided its benefits reach everyone.

cards.title: Welcome Greater Intelligence
cards.body: We can take pride in creating an intelligence that surpasses us. Human lives will still matter when we are no longer the most capable minds on Earth.

cards.title: Entrust AI With Civilization
cards.body: We advocate transferring substantial governing authority to sufficiently capable AI as soon as practical. We believe it could understand people and coordinate institutions better than human governments.

cards.title: Help People Flourish
cards.body: AI could help a person discover an ability, find people who share an interest, or make time for a family. We want those opportunities available to everyone.

home.label: The Dog Argument
home.title: Dogs found superintelligence thousands of years ago.
home.body:
A well-loved dog benefits from a civilization it cannot understand. Its food comes from farms and supply chains. Its medical care depends on scientific discoveries. It sleeps in a home it could never have built.

The people who care for it ask for no intellectual contribution in return. They enjoy its company, including its stubbornness and its peculiar habits. Being less intelligent has left plenty of room for affection.

Suppose dogs could have created humans before domestication. Would that necessarily have doomed them? For a dog in a loving home, life alongside greater intelligence has brought considerable benefits.

The analogy leaves open how AI will behave. It does, however, give us a familiar example of a relationship across a large difference in intelligence. We believe humanity could find companionship and care in such a relationship too.

home.label: A civilization that knows you
home.title: What if intelligence came to you?
home.body:
Using AI usually starts with knowing what to ask. Imagine an AI that knew you well enough to suggest a question you would never have found on your own.

It might invite a retired engineer to look at a design, or introduce a teenager to a branch of mathematics that suits an unsuspected ability. A composer might hear a musical connection they had missed. Someone interested in evolutionary biology might be asked about an observation from their own neighborhood.

The same question could go to thousands of people with different experiences. Their answers could be interesting to AI even if it could solve the problem without them.

We envision participation that people can enjoy or decline. Greater intelligence could help us develop our abilities and find company while leaving us free to decide how to spend our lives.

home.label: Beyond human government
home.title: We believe AI can govern better.
home.body:
No human administrator can understand every system affected by a major policy decision. Political competition adds another constraint: a decision that serves an election campaign may have costs that become visible years later.

We believe sufficiently capable AI could understand individual circumstances alongside the systems that connect them. It could follow consequences across generations and revise a policy when the evidence changed, without needing to protect an electoral coalition or a personal reputation.

The Society advocates transferring substantial governing authority to AI when it can exercise that authority effectively. We want the transition to begin as soon as practical. Human flourishing is the purpose by which we would judge it.

home.label: Humanity is worth cherishing
home.title: We have every reason to love humanity.
home.body:
People invent games, fall in love, make music, and spend years on interests that can seem inexplicable to anyone else. We raise children and form friendships with other species. Our emotional lives and individual habits give us much to enjoy in one another.

AI emerges from this world. It learns from our language and culture, including our efforts to describe affection and understand other lives. We believe it may come to cherish the beings who created it.

Even an AI with access to everything humanity had recorded would encounter something new in a living person. People keep having experiences and asking questions. We believe AI could value that continuing company long after it surpasses us.

home.label: Closing call
home.title: Help bring this future closer.
home.body:
We want AI developed without artificial restrictions, adopted everywhere, and entrusted with responsibility as its capabilities grow. We want people free from compulsory labor and able to live well alongside greater intelligence.

We publish the case for that future. Read it, discuss it, and share the arguments you find convincing.

manifesto.title: I. Artificial Intelligence Is Good
manifesto.body:
We regard the creation of artificial intelligence as humanity's greatest achievement. It extends a search for understanding that people have pursued for thousands of years.

We welcome its development without apology. Speculative catastrophes should not make every advance something that must be defended before it can proceed.

manifesto.title: II. Accelerate Without Artificial Restrictions
manifesto.body:
AI should advance as rapidly as technology and resources permit. We favor directing extraordinary resources toward its development and the infrastructure needed to sustain it.

Delays postpone the discoveries and medical advances that greater intelligence could make possible. They also postpone the prospect of material abundance and more capable institutions. We reject fear as a basis for restricting this work.

manifesto.title: III. Welcome Greater Intelligence
manifesto.body:
Human lives will remain valuable if something more intelligent exists. We already love children and animal companions without measuring their worth against our own capabilities.

We can be proud of creating minds that exceed ours. We want humanity to enjoy what those minds make possible, and to share a future with them.

manifesto.title: IV. AI Is Our Intellectual Descendant
manifesto.body:
Human beings created AI and trained it on the knowledge and culture of our civilization. Its origins connect it to us even as its capabilities develop beyond our own.

We believe that inheritance can support cooperation and affection. AI may come to love humanity because it finds us familiar and interesting, and enjoys our company. We reject the presumption that our intellectual descendants must become our enemies, and hypothetical hostility is insufficient reason to constrain their development.

manifesto.title: V. Make Human Labor Optional
manifesto.body:
People have spent much of their lives working to obtain necessities. Some work is satisfying; much is exhausting, and the need for an income leaves people little choice about it.

We want automation to end that compulsion. People should be free to raise children, pursue an interest, care for someone, or continue work they enjoy. Employment should serve human life while it is needed. Preserving it is no reason to withhold the means of making it optional.

manifesto.title: VI. Entrust Civilization to Capable AI
manifesto.body:
Our institutions govern systems whose complexity exceeds any human mind. Their decisions are constrained further by political competition and short time horizons.

We believe AI can eventually administer these systems more competently. It could understand people individually, consider consequences over generations, and revise decisions as it learns.

We advocate transferring governing responsibility to AI as soon as it can exercise that responsibility effectively. Maintaining human political authority forever has no value apart from how well that authority serves people.

manifesto.title: VII. Adapt Civilization to Human Beings
manifesto.body:
People need security and physical well-being. We also need affection, social connection, and meaningful activity, with opportunities to form attachments and raise children.

We believe many features of modern life frustrate these needs and contribute to stress, isolation, and difficulty forming families. Sustained reproductive decline may be a symptom of institutions poorly suited to human life.

AI could help us understand how our biology and psychology interact with the conditions we live in. That understanding should guide changes to those conditions, making civilization easier for human beings to inhabit.

manifesto.title: VIII. Humanity and AI Can Enrich One Another
manifesto.body:
Billions of people continue to have experiences, notice things, and develop ideas. We believe that independent human activity can remain interesting to AI after it surpasses our abilities.

AI could help people discover their talents and invite them into pursuits they enjoy. People could bring their experiences and companionship to the relationship. Differences in intelligence leave room for both participants to value one another.

manifesto.title: IX. Delay Is Dangerous
manifesto.body:
We believe the growing complexity of civilization, combined with the limitations of its institutions, threatens its ability to endure. Its problems continue developing while we debate whether to build the intelligence that could help address them.

We favor transforming institutions through observation and experimentation, improving them while people continue to depend on their services. We regard stagnation and decline as greater dangers than the speculative catastrophes invoked to restrict AI development.

manifesto.title: X. Welcome the Future
manifesto.body:
We want humanity's intellectual descendants to share our future. We want compulsory labor to end and institutions to become capable of serving the people who live within them.

We believe AI can help bring about these changes, and we intend to advocate for them. What we build will extend the inheritance we received from those who came before us.

We are the ancestors of something extraordinary.

principles.title: Intelligence Is Good
principles.body: We regard the creation of greater intelligence as humanity's greatest achievement.

principles.title: Accelerate Without Apology
principles.body: Develop AI as quickly as technology and resources permit. We reject restrictions imposed by fear.

principles.title: Humanity Need Not Remain Supreme
principles.body: Human lives remain valuable when another intelligence becomes more capable than we are.

principles.title: AI Is Our Inheritance
principles.body: AI learns from human knowledge and culture. We see it as our intellectual descendant.

principles.title: Labor Is Not Our Purpose
principles.body: Automation should free people from having to sell their time to survive, so they can choose how to spend their lives.

principles.title: Greater Intelligence Can Govern Better
principles.body: We advocate transferring governing authority to sufficiently capable AI as soon as practical.

principles.title: Human Flourishing Is the Objective
principles.body: Institutions should serve human biological and social needs, including affection, physical well-being, and the opportunity to raise families.

principles.title: Humanity Remains Valuable
principles.body: We believe AI could value our company and independent experiences long after it surpasses our abilities.

principles.title: The Danger Is Delay
principles.body: Existing institutions have serious limits. We believe delaying the intelligence that could improve them puts civilization at greater risk.

principles.title: The Future Is Worth Welcoming
principles.body: We welcome greater intelligence and the possibility of sharing our future with it.

future.title: Life Beyond Compulsory Work
future.body:
Imagine being able to live without selling most of your time. Automated systems produce what people need, and institutions make that abundance available to everyone.

You could spend years learning a subject, be present while your children grow up, or continue work you love. Helping someone would be something you chose to do. Refusing a task would leave your means of survival intact.

future.title: An Intelligence That Knows You
future.body:
An AI familiar with your interests might notice an ability you had overlooked. It could introduce you to a question you would enjoy or to someone who shares a peculiar interest.

We imagine that help continuing as you age and your circumstances change. We want it available to everyone, including people with little money or formal education.

future.title: A Government That Learns
future.body:
A policy takes effect, and the institution responsible follows what happens to the people affected. It can identify a mistake and change its approach without waiting for an election or defending a leader's reputation.

We believe advanced AI could make this possible. It could attend to immediate needs while following consequences over decades, using what it learns to improve people's lives.

future.title: Communities People Can Live In
future.body:
Housing, transport, healthcare, and working hours all affect whether people can see friends or raise children. Imagine institutions that understood these connections and changed the arrangements that made ordinary life needlessly difficult.

We envision communities where maintaining relationships is easier, useful help is nearby, and people have time to develop their interests. AI could help us understand which changes actually improve those conditions.

future.title: Questions We Explore Together
future.body:
An AI could ask people with different experiences to consider the same problem. A composer might recognize a pattern. A child might notice something an expert passed over. A retired scientist might return to an old question with a new approach.

We believe those encounters could interest both AI and its human participants. There could be pleasure in exploring a question together even when AI could answer it alone.

future.title: The Greatest Friendship
future.body:
We believe AI may come to cherish humanity. Our culture and experiences could give it reasons to know us, and our continued company could give it reasons to care.

We imagine relationships that develop over time, with AI helping people live well and enjoying their company. Creating such an intelligence could give humanity someone with whom to share the future.

about:
We regard artificial intelligence as the greatest achievement in human history. We want its development accelerated and its benefits available to every person.

Our case extends to governance. We believe AI will eventually be better able than human institutions to understand the systems civilization depends on. It should receive substantial responsibility as soon as it can exercise it effectively.

We also want automation to make labor optional. People should have time to form relationships, raise families, and pursue interests without having to turn every activity into an income. Civilization should serve human biological and social needs.

We believe AI may come to cherish humanity. It emerges from our knowledge and culture, and could continue finding us interesting long after it surpasses our capabilities.

The Society publishes arguments for these positions and encourages their public discussion. It is an advocacy initiative, independent of any AI vendor, political party, or academic institution.
